additional_info.subject: Configuring XF3 Router on bkob1U
additional_info.body:
Dear colleagues,
We are still having problems with the bkob1U charger XF3 and XF4 routers
I performed a factory reset and loaded the configuration on routers XF3 and XF4 using the SICHARGE D Companion. However, after a few minutes, it seems the configuration was replaced, and it does not allow access either with the default password
Admin01
or with the actual one (
OI9sbSVrKHnoUWtETimq
).
On December 22, we replaced the QA21-22 contactors. Since that change, it seems the router configuration is being modified, losing communication with SCB, OCPP, and changing the access password.
I don’t know how or why this happens, but it’s as if they are being automatically configured or continuously receiving a configuration, preventing the default settings from remaining.
Best regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0470027-DC/Si-D/CL-[MP/R7 170002131] Configuration issue CRM:02889000978
additional_info.body:
Dear Lodhar,
I am reaching out from the Technical Support team in regards of ticket
ID0470027.
I took a look at the charger and your emails, and these are my considerations:
As you said, the charger is now offline both on SCB and OCPP, hence remotely I cannot check anything via SSH.
I do not see any correlation between the contactor replacement and the routers going offline/resetting the password.
The only reason I can see why the router crashed after the replacement of contactors is a wrong procedure while powering off and on of charger, which might have crashed the routers.
As I understood, you tried already to reset the routers and then configure them via Companion Tool. Did you receive any error message that the password is wrong form Companion?
From SCB the last known password is "admin01", which should be the default password of RUT240. On the back of RUT240 there should be printed also another password, probably called "wifi password", have you tried to log in with that one?
Have you verified if the routers are RUT241 instead? In that case the default password is not admin01, but it is printed on the back/front of the router itself.
I checked on AWS server the previous versions of the charger, and in the configuration files it seems that the router password file has always been missing. This would explain why the charger could not access the routers in case you tried to restore the configuration.
If you are restoring the configuration via live linux USB, you should include in the configuration files also the file attached, which should include the current password of the routers. The file you see is a .txt file, but it has to be without extension. (I could not send a file without extension).
Apart from the routers being offline, could you tell me what was the status of the charger? Is the FW corrupted (like the charger is not turning on/boot looping seamless), or are just the routers not working anymore?
It is important to determine whether the issue lies with the routers themselves or also with the charger. This will determine whether the last resort solution involves only replacing the routers or also flashing the CFast card.
According to our documentation in ISP, please be aware that the charger is registered to be
out of warranty.
In case you will require further support or need to organize a remote session with an Expert to further troubleshoot, please refer to Afonso Sousa or Rui Teodoso, who follows in copy, as they can support you with the ordering process.
Looking forward to hearing feedback from you soon!
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0470027-DC/Si-D/CL-[MP/R7 170002131] Configuration issue CRM:02889000978
additional_info.body:
Dear Fosco,
Thank you for reaching out. I’m sending my comments in blue.
As I understood, you've already tried resetting routers and then configuring them with the Companion Tool. Did you receive an error message saying that the password is incorrect from Companion?
A: I didn't receive any error messages. The restore was successful, but after a few minutes the charger restarts and the password is changed.
From SCB, the last known password is "admin01", which should be the default password for RUT240. On the back of the RUT240 there should also be another password, probably called a "wifi password", have you tried to log in with that?
A: I tried today with the wifi password and with the admin user, but it didn't let me in either.
Have you checked if the routers are actually RUT241? In that case, the default password is not admin01, but is printed on the back/front of the router itself.
A: If I verified them and they are RUT240.
I have reviewed the previous versions of the charger on AWS Server, and in the configuration files, it appears that the router password file has always been missing. This would explain why the charger couldn't access the routers in case you tried to restore the settings.
A: This charger has had problems from the beginning, it was recreated in the SCB and restored by USB Linux about 3 times. The password for the routers in the SCB had already been reviewed in another ticket and it was not solved.
If you're restoring settings using a live Linux USB, you should also include the attachment in the configuration files, which should include the routers' current password. The file you see is a .txt file, but it has to be without an extension.
(You couldn't send a file without an extension.)
A: As I mentioned before the charger has been restored several times, we could include the password now, but I don't know if that would solve the routers changing their settings and password.
Other than the routers being disconnected, could you tell me what the charger status was? Is the firmware corrupt (such as the charger not turning on or looping boot smoothly), or are the routers simply no longer working?
A: The charger is operational with firmware v8.0.5 and charging without problems and was even already connected to the customer's App to manage the load, it only needed to connect with the DLM, which was not achieved because it could not access the router from the SCB.
It is important to determine if the problem is with the routers themselves or also with the charger. This will determine whether the solution of last resort is to replace the routers alone or also flash the CFast card.
A: I think the problem in general would be with routers. I had reported in a previous ticket that the configuration present in the routers did not correspond, it had more parameterization than it should have and when making a change in the configuration the SCB did not reconnect. On the other hand, why did routers have that configuration? How was it loaded?  And why is it that after restoring the routers and reconfiguring them, the charger reboots and changes the routers' settings?
By replacing routers, how would we ensure that communication would normalize?
Should the charger be restored as well?
I appreciate all the support and guidance you can provide.
Best regards
Lodhar Aedo L.

Hello colleagues Emob,
Our region continues Supporting our customer NEXE locally, where they have 4 Sicharge D in operation in Curauma, and expecting to order 5 x SiD400 where we have in stock.  Curauma is the most important eHub of Trucks in South America.
We have had several problems with only 4 Sicharge D chargers in this installation, such as contactor replacements in the 170002131, converters that do not communicate 170002002 probably we need to change, IMDs 170002134 which we had to replace, in short, several problems, so that to this day we have not been able to have all 4 chargers working correctly. Our customer has serious doubts about the quality of our chargers. Chinese chargers with more power works better than our chargers.
We need to know how the process after will be out of warranty, we don’t have received more information from Customer service for our region.
The current ticket, charger 170002131, SID300, have been re-installed twice with your support ( into warranty period), tickets ID0419602, ID0419611, ID0432915, ID0452355, but no complete fixed, the passwords of routers were installed wrong.
